name: TX-08
label: Safe R

key_factors: Huge GOP fundraising and outside-spending advantage
Open seat removes incumbent benefit but not structural lean
model.rationale: The district's R+13 lean, the Republican nominee's $2M-plus in fundraising with $1.7M in outside support against a Democratic rival who raised about $22K, and prediction markets pricing Republican odds near 95% all point to a comfortable GOP hold. The open seat adds some uncertainty but does not change the fundamentals.
model.watch: Any late surge in Democratic fundraising or outside spending, or an unexpected scandal involving the Republican nominee, could narrow the margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Morgan Luttrell (R) is not on the ballot.

overview:
TX-08 is a solidly Republican Houston-area seat, with a partisan lean of about 13 points toward the GOP. Morgan Luttrell is retiring, so this is an open-seat contest between Republican Jessica Hart Steinmann and Democrat Laura Jones. No public general-election polls are available, and no expert raters cover the race.

The financial picture is lopsided: Steinmann has raised over $2 million and benefits from roughly $1.7 million in outside support, while Jones has raised about $22,000 with no reported outside spending. Prediction markets give the Democrat roughly a 4% chance. The forecast expects a Republican hold by a wide, though not landslide, margin, with moderate uncertainty given the absence of polling.
